questions.q: What is React? What is the Role of React in software development?

answer.value: React is an open-source front-end JavaScript library developed by Meta. Its primary role in software development is to build dynamic, high-performance User Interfaces (UIs) using a component-based architecture.
Real-life / project example: A component describes reusable UI. React updates the UI when its data changes.

answer.title: Practical example

questions.q: What are the Key Features of React?

answer.value: Key features include Component-Based Architecture, Virtual DOM, JSX (JavaScript XML), Unidirectional Data Flow, and a robust ecosystem supporting state management and routing.
Real-life / project example: For example, a product card can be built once and reused for every product.

answer.title: Practical example

questions.q: What is DOM? What is the difference between HTML and DOM?

answer.value: The DOM (Document Object Model) is a programming interface representing web pages as a tree structure of objects. HTML is the textual document format used to write layouts, while the DOM is the active, live object tree memory representation generated by the browser from that HTML.
Real-life / project example: When a value changes, React renders the component description again and reconciles it with the previous tree.

questions.q: What is Virtual DOM? Difference between DOM and Virtual DOM?

answer.value: The Virtual DOM is a lightweight, in-memory copy of the real DOM. When updates occur, React alters the Virtual DOM first, runs a diffing algorithm, and patches only the changed nodes onto the real DOM, making it significantly faster than direct real DOM manipulation.

answer.alt: State change creates a new Virtual DOM, which is diffed and applied to the Real DOM
answer.caption: Virtual DOM update flow

answer.value: Mention the **diffing (reconciliation)** step in interviews — it is what most candidates miss.
Real-life / project example: When a value changes, React renders the component description again and reconciles it with the previous tree.

questions.q: What are React Components? What are the main elements of it?

answer.value: React Components are reusable, self-contained UI building blocks. The main elements composing a component are State (internal memory), Props (external configuration inputs), and a Return statement specifying the layout via JSX.
Real-life / project example: A reusable profile component can display different users using props.

questions.q: What is SPA(Single Page Application)?

answer.value: An SPA is a web application that loads a single HTML page. Subsequent interaction dynamically rewrites the page via JavaScript API calls rather than forcing the browser to download entirely new pages from a server.

questions.q: What are Pure and Impure functions in JS?

answer.value: Pure functions always return the exact same output when given the same inputs and cause zero side effects. Impure functions modify external variables or rely on outside data changes, making their outputs unpredictable.

questions.q: What are template literals and string interpolation in strings?

questions.q: What is asynchronous programming in JS? What is its use?

answer.value: A non-blocking execution model that lets your app kick off long-running operations (like network requests) and keep running other code in the meantime, handling the results whenever the task completes.

questions.q: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous programming?

answer.value: Synchronous operations run strictly step-by-step, blocking any further code execution until the current line finishes. Asynchronous operations run in the background, letting the main code pipeline continue running without interruption.

questions.q: What are Promises in JavaScript?

answer.value: A Promise is an object representing the eventual completion (or failure) of an asynchronous operation, existing in one of three states: Pending, Fulfilled, or Rejected.

questions.q: What is Typescript? Or What is the difference between Typescript and Javascript?

answer.value: TypeScript is a strongly typed superset of JavaScript developed by Microsoft. It adds optional static typing to the language, catching type errors during development before the code is compiled down to standard JavaScript.

questions.q: What is the difference between void and never types in Typescript?

answer.value: void means a function executes successfully but does not return a value. never means a function can never finish executing, either because it loops infinitely or throws a runtime error.

questions.q: What's the difference between extends and implements in TypeScript?

answer.value: extends is used when a child class inherits from a parent class or when an interface inherits from another interface. implements is used when a class signs up to follow a structural contract defined by an interface.

questions.q: Is Multiple Inheritance possible in Typescript?
